Q: When should I use a Binary Tree in Python, and what problems does it solve? A:

It is also worth mentioning binary heaps, a type of binary tree that allows you to quickly extract the minimum or maximum element.

Practical example:
Let n athletes take part in the competition. You need to display only the m athletes with the best results in the table. There are two ways you can do this:

  1. Sort an array of n elements and take the first m elements. The time complexity is O(n log n + 1) (for n = 1000, m = 10 requires ~9967 operations).
  2. Make a heap of n elements and extract m elements. The time complexity is O(n + m log n) (for n = 1000, m = 10 requires ~1033 operations).

Q: Run-time error after switching Redshfit ODBC-Driver 1.0 to ODBC-Driver 2.0 A:

Do it this way;

Sub Diagnose_Fields()
    Dim conn As New ADODB.Connection
    Dim rs   As New ADODB.Recordset
    Dim f    As ADODB.Field

    conn.ConnectionString = "DRIVER={Amazon Redshift ODBC Driver (x64)};" & _
                            "Server=xx; Database=xx; UID=xx; PWD=xx;"
    conn.CursorLocation = adUseClient
    conn.Open

    Dim strSQL As String
    strSQL = Sheet1.Shapes("SqlQuery1").OLEFormat.Object.Text

    rs.Open strSQL, conn, adOpenStatic, adLockReadOnly

    For Each f In rs.Fields
        Debug.Print f.Name & " | ADO Type: " & f.Type & " | Size: " & f.DefinedSize
    Next f

    rs.Close
    conn.Close
End Sub

Check the Immediate window (Ctrl+G). Any field with ADO type 201 (adLongVarChar), 205 (adLongVarBinary), or an unusual large size is the likely culprit.

Fix: Replace CopyFromRecordset with a safe array write

GetRows() pulls the data into a Variant array without the type-mapping restrictions of CopyFromRecordset. This is a drop-in replacement that handles any column type:

Sub Query_Data_Driver2()
    Dim conn As New ADODB.Connection
    Dim rs As New ADODB.Recordset

    conn.ConnectionString = "DRIVER={Amazon Redshift ODBC Driver (x64)};Server=xx;Database=xx;UID=xx;PWD=xx;"
    conn.CursorLocation = adUseClient
    conn.Open

    Dim strSQL As String
    strSQL = Sheet1.Shapes("SqlQuery1").OLEFormat.Object.Text

    rs.Open strSQL, conn, adOpenStatic, adLockReadOnly

    If Not (rs.BOF And rs.EOF) Then
        PasteRecordset rs, Sheet1.Range("A1")
    End If

    rs.Close
    conn.Close
End Sub

Private Sub PasteRecordset(rs As ADODB.Recordset, startCell As Range)
    Dim raw() As Variant
    Dim out() As Variant
    Dim nCols As Long, nRows As Long
    Dim r As Long, c As Long
    Dim v As Variant

    raw = rs.GetRows()
    nCols = UBound(raw, 1) + 1
    nRows = UBound(raw, 2) + 1
    ReDim out(1 To nRows, 1 To nCols)

    For r = 1 To nRows
        For c = 1 To nCols
            v = raw(c - 1, r - 1)
            Select Case VarType(v)
                Case vbNull:            out(r, c) = ""
                Case vbObject, vbArray: out(r, c) = CStr(v)
                Case Else:              out(r, c) = v
            End Select
        Next c
    Next r

    startCell.Resize(nRows, nCols).Value = out
End Sub
